vespers noun

also evening service, evening prayer, evensong

medieval

the Roman Breviary’s ad Vesperās

vesperae, vesperārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

The evening office of East and West alike. In the Byzantine rite it begins the liturgical day, and Ps. 140 (141) is its lamp-lighting psalm; in the West the Magnificat is sung at Vespers. Classical vespera is the evening itself (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • lucernāre, lucernāris n. — the lamp-lighting service, vespers

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Egeria, Itin. 25: et ad lucernāre jūxtā cōnsuētūdinem cotīdiānam fit · Declension on Wiktionary

    Egeria’s word for the evening service at Jerusalem, from lucernāris, of lamps (Lewis & Short).

  • officium vespertīnum — the evening office

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. service: vespers (Tursellinus, 1652)

Examples

  • Dīrigātur ōrātiō mea sīcut incēnsum in cōnspectū tuō; ēlevātiō manuum meārum sacrificium vespertīnum.

    Let my prayer rise like incense before you, the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.Vulg. Ps. 140 (141), 2

See also matins, prayer, church.
